video.hook: the seesaw starts level with the first steel ball already on the zigzag; it lands and tips the beam at 0.6 s
video.structure: glass marbles arrive in three waves (8, 10, 12) and steel balls one at a time; the beam changes sides 7 times; after all 30 glass are in, steel needs all 10 and the 10th tips it; then STEEL WINS!, a crown over the basket and the fun fact
video.model: the co-owner's 18 GLASS vs 2 STEEL balance Short, made physically correct (same-size steel is 3.14 times heavier than glass, so 2 steel balls can't beat 18 glass marbles)

physics.contacts: soft spheres: stiffness 2.5e5 per unit mass, damping 0.55 (walls) / 0.5 (marbles) of critical; rolling resistance 3 units/s2 on wood; marble-on-marble friction 0.15
physics.beam: turned by the vertical push of every marble on a basket at the fixed arm (like a scale pan), plus bearing friction and the stop posts at +-8 deg
physics.front_pane: the baskets' low front walls are full height in the physics only (like clear panes), so a tall pile can't spill toward the camera

render.poses: beam angle rounded to 0.15 deg (slow), 0.3 (medium) or 0.6 (fast); each pose path-traces only the window the seesaw changes (41% of the image), feathered 40 px into the level set

steel.reflection: dark band at the horizon, bright room above

text.watermark: Marble Pop at 0.968 of the height

sound.bed: suspense pulse 128 BPM, louder for the last steel ball, with a riser into the tip
sound.glass: bright clinks between glass marbles, light wooden knocks
sound.steel: metallic rings between steel balls, heavier knocks and a thunk when one lands
sound.beam: a deep wooden thunk each time the beam lands on a stop post
sound.rolling: noise through wood resonances 700/1400/3100 Hz following the rolling marbles
sound.winner: brass fanfare, crash, six claps, then a happy loop at 118 BPM
